_note: Clinical Intelligence is decision support with a doctor's signature: the clinical inbox, review and sign, structured consultations, triage on ratified protocols, result acknowledgement, Home Guidance and PROMs. Every protocol in packages/catalog/protocols.json is a draft today, so every triage and guidance call is refused in practice until the board ratifies one. Wave 2 contract; built on the engine runtime in Wave 5, when the inbox, the signature, the consultation, triage and outcome questions were withdrawn for versions that refuse what the first could not. packages/catalog/clinical.json holds the frames, registries, words and settings.

refusals.statement: Nothing is triaged without a ratified protocol.
refusals.why: Software does not triage until the board has ratified the rules it triages by.

refusals.statement: No model output lowers a priority the rules set.
refusals.why: §15D: generative AI may explain a priority; it may not lower one.

refusals.statement: No output tells a patient they have a condition.
refusals.why: Findings are "consistent with", for a clinician to confirm (§5.3).

refusals.statement: Nothing is signed automatically.
refusals.why: A note is signed by a doctor's own action.

refusals.statement: A result is not complete until a clinician acknowledges it.
refusals.why: An unacknowledged result is a loop nobody closed.

refusals.statement: That rota leaves hours uncovered that must always have somebody on them.

refusals.statement: A clinical review says why the value is safe, or it is not recorded.
refusals.why: A confirmation with no reason is a signature under nothing.

refusals.statement: That is not the value in force for this setting. Review what is in force now.
refusals.why: A reviewer confirms the value they read. A value replaced since is not the one patients are being treated under.

refusals.statement: That value has already been clinically reviewed.
refusals.why: Two confirmations of one value are one review recorded twice.

refusals.statement: Nobody confirms the clinical review of a change they made themselves.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/vetting.json's selfActionRefusals, applied to settings: a review by the person who made the change is no review.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: A confirmation changes no value, so nothing acts differently because of it. It is the row it appends to the engine's own reviews, which the read route returns.

routes.summary: Read the Clinician Review Queue: every proposed change to Tier 1 global escalation behaviour, a tenant's Tier 2 additive layer, or a device threshold rule, by reference and state. Carries none of the change's own content, per packages/catalog/clinical-review-queue.json whereContentLives.

request.why: Filter by 1, 2 or device.
Filter to one tenant's Tier 2 entries.
Filter by state, from packages/catalog/clinical-review-queue.json states.

response.why: Queue entries.

refusals.statement: That is not a state an entry can be in.
refusals.why: A filter on an undeclared state answers an empty queue, which reads as nothing proposed.

routes.summary: Propose a change to Tier 1, a tenant's Tier 2 layer, or a device threshold rule. Enters the queue as proposed and decides nothing until ratified.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same proposal once.
1, 2 or device, from packages/catalog/clinical-review-queue.json tiers.
Required for a Tier 2 entry, refused if present for Tier 1.
Where the change is written. Never the change's own content.
What the proposal cites. A proposal with nothing behind it is refused.

response.why: The queue entry created.
Always proposed on creation.

refusals.statement: That is not a tier this queue accepts.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/clinical-review-queue.json names exactly three.

refusals.statement: A Tier 2 entry names the tenant it applies to.
refusals.why: A tenantless Tier 2 entry cannot be checked against that tenant's own Tier 1 boundary.

refusals.statement: A Tier 1 entry names no tenant. It is global.
refusals.why: A Tier 1 change scoped to one tenant would not be the global core it claims to be.

refusals.statement: A proposal cites what it is based on, or it is not recorded.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/clinical-review-queue.json refusals: a-proposed-entry-carries-no-authority — and an unevidenced one is not worth the board's time to refuse a second way.

routes.summary: Move a proposed entry to in-review, naming who is looking at it. Decides nothing; a reviewed entry still carries no authority until signed.

request.why: The entry, from the path.
Chosen by the caller.

response.why: The entry.
Always in-review on success.

refusals.statement: Only a vetted clinician holding the sign-clinical-review capability the settings in force name moves an entry to review.
refusals.why: Reviewing a proposal to change clinical behaviour is a clinician's act, the same standing packages/catalog/clinical.json already requires to sign a review.

refusals.statement: Only a proposed entry may move to in-review.
refusals.why: An entry already reviewed, ratified, rejected or rolled back has already moved past this step, and moving it again would be a second history for the same entry.

refusals.statement: Nobody reviews a change they proposed themselves.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/vetting.json's selfActionRefusals, applied to the queue: a review by the proposer is no review.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: Moving an entry to in-review carries no authority and decides nothing a subscriber would act on; only ratification and rejection are worth announcing.

routes.summary: Ratify or reject an in-review entry, by name, role and day. Only a ratified entry may ever be cited as the reason a clinical behaviour changed.

request.why: The entry, from the path.
Chosen by the caller.
ratified or rejected.
Why. Required either way, so a rejection is as traceable as a ratification.

response.why: The entry.
ratified or rejected.
Role, name and day, matching packages/catalog/protocols.json's ratification shape.

refusals.statement: Only a vetted clinician holding the sign-clinical-review capability the settings in force name signs an entry.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/clinical-review-queue.json refusals: no-signature-no-ratification.

refusals.statement: Only an in-review entry may be ratified or rejected.
refusals.why: Signing a proposed entry would skip the board looking at it; signing a ratified one twice would be two signatures for one decision.

refusals.statement: This Tier 2 entry removes, weakens or overrides a Tier 1 rule, and is refused rather than ratified.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/clinical-review-queue.json refusals: tier-2-may-not-subtract. Caught again here because a proposal can be well-evidenced and still subtract; ratification is the last gate before it would take effect.

refusals.statement: The clinical governance board packages/catalog/protocols.json#governance records is not-formed, and its Medical Director is not-appointed. Nothing may be ratified until both exist.
refusals.why: A ratification under an authority this file admits does not yet exist would be exactly the borrowed authority packages/catalog/protocols.json was written to refuse.

routes.summary: Propose reverting a live entry. Creates a new entry naming the one it would revert; the live entry itself is never edited or removed. The new entry is proposed, reviewed and ratified exactly like any other change before the rollback takes effect.

request.why: The live entry to revert, from the path.
Chosen by the caller.
Why this is being reverted.

response.why: The new entry created.
The live entry it would revert.
Always proposed on creation — a rollback is not itself live until it, too, is ratified.

refusals.statement: Only a live entry may be named as the target of a rollback.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/clinical-review-queue.json refusals: rollback-is-a-new-row. Reverting a proposal, a rejection or an already-rolled-back entry is not a rollback of anything in effect.

refusals.statement: A rollback cites why it is being reverted, or it is not recorded.
refusals.why: Reverting a live clinical rule is itself a clinical change, held to the same evidence requirement as the rule it undoes.

routes.summary: Open a case from a completed symptom intake: the Passport entry the answers were written to, the readings Devices was asked about, and the preview pathway's suggestion worked out once from them. The patient asked for a nurse to look at the notes; nothing is opened without that.

request.why: Whose case, by the patient's opaque reference. The caller's own session must be the subject's.

The intake group the answers were gathered under, from packages/catalog/symptom-intake.json groups. Only a group with questionsFrom opens a case: the pathway is derived from the knowledge base, and a group without that derivation has no pathway.

The Health Passport entry the answers were written to under the patient's own grant, through the consent gateway. Clinical reads the answers through the gateway to work out the features and the findings, and keeps the reference.

The readings Devices was asked about for this case, by reference, or an empty list. The values are Observations in the Passport; Devices holds each reading's source, quality and marks, which decide its weight.
Whether the intake ended on an emergency word. True opens the case in the emergency state, kept rather than deleted, and the suggestion is the emergency answer.

response.why: The case.
Opened, or emergency, from packages/catalog/case.json states.
The preview pathway the suggestion was made under.
Whether the register holds that pathway as ratified today. False: it is a draft, and every screen says so.

Where the pathway suggests the patient is seen, from packages/catalog/case.json settings.kinds. For the nurse's screen; never returned to a patient's client, which the patient caller's response leaves out by the neverToPatient rule.
Which rule of the pathway matched, from packages/catalog/case.json pathway.rules, so the nurse reads the reason in the contract's words.

refusals.statement: That complaint has no pathway yet. The notes stay with the patient for the visit.
refusals.why: Only a group derived from the knowledge base (symptom-intake.json questionsFrom) carries features and findings a pathway can read. A case on any other group would be a case with nothing in it but answers.

refusals.statement: A case opens on a completed intake. Nothing was gathered for a nurse yet.
refusals.why: The pathway reads every answer. A case opened half-way through the questions would suggest a setting from half the notes.

refusals.statement: A case is opened by the patient asking for a nurse to look at the notes, and by nothing else.
refusals.why: The notes are the patient's until they say so. GilbertOne finishing the questions is not the patient asking for a nurse.

refusals.statement: A reading in a case is one Devices was asked about, by reference. A value is not accepted here.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/devices.json whereValuesLive: the value is written to the Passport by the capturer, and Devices keeps the source, the sample and the marks that decide its weight. A case that took a value would be a second store for readings.

routes.summary: Read a case file: its state, its answers by Passport reference, its readings by reference with the weight Devices gives each, what the notes are consistent with, the pathway's suggestion with its reason, every decision with the role that made it, and the consultation reference once a doctor has signed. A patient reads their own case without the findings or the suggestion.

request.why: The case.

response.why: The case.
Whose case, by opaque reference.
From packages/catalog/case.json states.
The intake group the answers were gathered under.
The Passport entry holding the answers, read under the reader's own grant.
The readings in the case, by reference. Their weight is Devices' answer for each, read by reference.

The finding rules that matched, from packages/catalog/case.json findings.rules, each of which names its condition ids. For a nurse or a doctor; left out of a patient's answer by the neverToPatient rule.
The preview pathway.
False while it is a draft. Every screen reads the banner from it.
Where the pathway suggested. Left out of a patient's answer.
The rule that matched. Left out of a patient's answer.
Every decision on the case, oldest first, each with the role that made it.

fields.why: Who decided: patient, nurse or doctor, by role and never by name.
What was decided: opened, took, confirmed, overrode, repeated-reading, handed-over or closed.
The setting decided, from packages/catalog/case.json settings.kinds, for a confirmation or an override.
The nurse's reason for choosing differently from the suggestion, in her words. Present only on an override.
When.

response.why: The signed consultation, once a doctor closed the case; null before.
The Home Guidance outcome the doctor recorded, from packages/catalog/clinical.json guidance.outcomes; null before.

refusals.statement: There is no case by that reference.
refusals.why: A reference nobody opened reads as nothing rather than as an empty case.

refusals.statement: A patient reads their own case and nobody else's.
refusals.why: The session's subject must be the case's. A case is a patient's notes about their own body.

refusals.statement: What the notes are consistent with, and where the pathway suggested, are read by a nurse or a doctor. They are not returned to a patient.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/clinical.json wording: a finding is consistent with something for a clinician to confirm. Returned to a patient it would read as what they have, with nobody accountable for saying so.

routes.summary: A nurse decides where the patient is seen: confirming the preview pathway's suggestion, or choosing a different setting with her reason. Software suggested; she decides, and the decision is hers by registration.

request.why: The case.
Where the patient is seen, from packages/catalog/case.json settings.kinds.
Required when the setting is not the one the pathway suggested. Her words, written on the case.

response.why: The case.
The state the decision put the case in: home-visit, online, self-care or emergency.
Whether she chose differently from the suggestion.
When.

refusals.statement: There is no case by that reference.
refusals.why: As on the read.

refusals.statement: A setting is decided on a case a nurse has taken and nobody has decided yet.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/case.json transitions: the decision is made once, from with-nurse. A second decision is a new case or a doctor's, never an edit.

refusals.statement: That is not a setting a patient can be seen in.
refusals.why: Only the four packages/catalog/case.json declares. A setting nobody declared has no outcome mapped to it and no words on any screen.

refusals.statement: A setting other than the suggested one needs the nurse's reason, in her words.
refusals.why: The suggestion is a draft's; her decision overrides it by her authority, and the record must say why so the doctor and the board can read it.

refusals.statement: Only a vetted nurse decides where a patient is seen on a case.
refusals.why: The founder's design: GilbertOne gathers, the nurse decides where, the doctor decides what. Software never decides this, and a patient does not decide it for themselves here.
